items.article_search_text: Formula 1 fans were left star-struck after spotting Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Oscar Piastri at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Monday (Sept 28), ahead of this weekend's race at Sepang International Circuit.Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto was also reportedly spotted, along with engineers and staff from teams including McLaren, Red Bull and Audi.Netizens took to social media to... Formula 1 fans were left star-struck after spotting Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Oscar Piastri at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Monday (Sept 28), ahead of this weekend's race at Sepang International Circuit. Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto was also reportedly spotted, along with engineers and staff from teams including McLaren, Red Bull and Audi. Netizens took to social media to share their excitement, with pictures and videos of the drivers. "Oscar has landed in Malaysia!" wrote laurogeitabat on Threads, adding that the 25-year-old stopped for pictures and autographs. The video, posted on Monday, shows the Australian driver posing for a selfie with a fan before heading towards the airport exit with his entourage. Antonelli was also seen waving at fans and stopping for a photo while manoeuvring his luggage in a separate video posted to Threads by sec_hann28 on Sept 28. The Italian currently leads the Formula One Drivers' Championship with 302 points, while Mercedes teammate George Russell is in second place, with 236 points. The drivers flew into Kuala Lumpur from Baku following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where Russell claimed victory ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Antonelli finished fifth. "We met Gabriel Bortoleto," Threads user nr.suriana wrote on Monday, sharing a video of the Audi driver noticing them and waving in their direction. Besides the faces of F1, fans also gushed over the engineers and staff members from the various teams. "It's a beautiful night when you accidentally arrived [at] the same time as McLaren, Williams, Haas, Audi, Red Bull engineers and staff," wrote fionanhy on Threads at 3am on Monday with a video of a throng of people waiting with their luggage. She added that the race in Malaysia is "getting real". Threads user f1leaks.my also posted on Sept 28 that engineers and staff from Alpine, Aston Martine and Cadillac were amongst those that had arrived in Kuala Lumpur. The Formula One race at Sepang International Circuit, scheduled for Oct 2 to 4, marks the championship's return to Malaysia for the first time since 2017. Although held in Malaysia, the event will officially be known as the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix after Formula One relocated the race from its original venue amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

items.article_search_text: The McLaren driver explained why he failed to score points at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. McLaren driver Oscar Piastri made a serious mistake late in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix while battling for points.The Australian locked both front wheels simultaneously on lap 40 as he approached Turn 1. The incident occurred while he was trying to defend his position from Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar. Piastri had been running second until that point and had managed to keep Max Verstappen behind him through lap 30.The safety car was deployed after Alex Albon’s crash. Piastri failed to maintain his position after the restart and dropped back following the incident one lap after the second restart, eventually finishing the race in 13th place.Piastri explained his mistake as follows: “It was a bit strange. Both front wheels locked up at once. While defending, I was on a different line from the one I usually use. I don’t know whether I went over a bump, but it came as a surprise to me.”He said the weekend as a whole had been more encouraging than the previous races. Piastri added that he had been able to extract more lap-time performance from the car and had gained a better understanding of the areas in which he needed to improve his driving style.“Apart from one episode in the race, I was closer to the level I expected of myself this weekend. That is more encouraging in this regard. But not getting anything in return for it yet hurts a lot,” he added.Piastri’s 13th-place finish and Lando Norris’ early retirement meant McLaren left Baku without points. The team also suffered an additional setback in its battle with Ferrari for second place in the Constructors’ Championship.The Azerbaijan Grand Prix is held on Baku’s street circuit, where narrow sections and heavy braking zones can make defending positions particularly demanding. items.article_search_text: The Azerbaijan GP where Oscar Piastri's title hopes started to sink in 2025 has haunted the Australian again... Oscar Piastri's Baku misery has resurfaced again with the Australian guilty of what a former world champ called a "rookie mistake", blowing the chance of a podium finish while George Russell completed an immaculate lights-to-flag victory in the crashed-marred Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Piastri, whose championship hopes began to crumble last year when he crashed on the tight road circuit with which he's had a "love-hate relationship", this time locked up with third place in his grasp with 10 laps left on Saturday and slid straight into the run-off. By the time he got back on track, he was 15th, his hopes of any points gone, and he ended up 14th, with McLaren suffering double woe after Lando Norris had earlier crashed out, maddened at being the innocent victim in a multiple crash caused by Franco Colapinto. Up ahead, Russell, who led from start to finish and survived the pressure of two restarts under the safety car, held off Max Verstappen in a dramatic finish to win his first race for three months and cut into Mercedes' teammate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead. Russell managed to defend from Verstappen, who charged from eighth through to second, despite his Mercedes losing power in the denouement as Valtteri Bottas's last-lap crash in his Cadillac forced both the leaders to slow as the finish line approached. At the end, Russell had less than two-tenths of a second to spare over his old rival, a margin rather smaller than he'd won his pole by in qualifying. "I lost the boost, I had no power. Thought he was going to get us," a relieved Russell said. Verstappen's Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar was third in a superb return from injury. Antonelli, who'd started 16th after a qualifying crash, ended up battling his way through to fifth, limiting the damage to his title lead as he's still 66 points ahead. But Piastri couldn't hide his disappointment at the miserable conclusion to what had been a weekend when he'd seemingly rekindled his 'love' for the track where he'd won in 2024. On the soft tyres, he'd whipped past Ferrari's Charles Leclerc at the start to grab second place and then held off the challenge of the Red Bulls impressively. But after Alex Albon went into the wall on lap 31 and Piastri found himself on the mediums after everyone pitted under the yellow flag, he was picked off immediately by Verstappen on the restart. Then, with the race having to be restarted again once Colapinto caused the crash which took out both his Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly and Norris, Piastri bemoaned his slide-off error while under pressure from Hadjar. The mistake didn't impress outspoken 1997 world champion Jacques Villeneuve, who told Sky Sports: "It was a rookie mistake. He got caught out, looking in his mirrors, and just completely missed." Piastri's view was, unsurprisingly, different. "I didn't think I braked super-late or super-hard, but just instantly locked both fronts," said the Victorian. "It certainly took me by surprise, "Just a disappointing end to the day. The first half of the race was very strong, so it's a shame not to have anything to show for it." Norris had been left dismayed by his race ending because Colapinto locked up while ploughing recklessly down the inside after the safety-car restart, an error which the Argentine apologised for profusely. Norris, though, muttered darkly: "Just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula One to be honest." He felt the Argentine should get a one-race ban because "that's not driving that deserves to be in Formula One", but both Verstappen and Russell felt that a suspension would be too harsh. George Russell starts on pole for the first time since Austria in June - and that was his last win too. Can he get his title challenge back on track today? There’s a very good opportunity to take a chunk out of Kimi Antonelli’s 81-point lead, with the Italian starting in 16th. How quickly can he move up the order? And what about Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull? Leclerc is in P2, with Piastri P3 and Hadjar an impressive P4. Oscar Piastri, who starts P3: 11:54 , Kieran Jackson “We looked pretty good on Thursday so hopefully we can keep that going but I think to be quick by yourself is one thing; to be able to overtake people is another, so we’ll see what we get."I’m expecting George to drive off into the distance and I think we’ll be looking at Kimi in our mirrors pretty quickly." Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur: 11:51 , Kieran Jackson “Even if you’re in front at end of lap one, might not be in front at start of lap two... we’ll just see at the end!” Time for the Azerbaijan national anthem 11:46 , Kieran Jackson Genuinely one of my favourite anthems on the calendar! I’m feeling confident. I think we’ve got great pace beneath us."I think the race start is going to be key. I’m sure Charles is going to be pretty motivated to overtake at the beginning."But I’m confident if I can get the lead, I can try to pull that gap and control the race." This week has definitely been more competitive.” Lewis Hamilton after qualifying in sixth: 11:18 , Kieran Jackson “Q1 was fairly solid and there were some positive elements to take from the session. However, getting the tyre temperatures right was a challenge throughout qualifying and that made it difficult to consistently get them into the right operating window. “We struggled to extract the grip we were looking for, particularly in Q3, and not having a tow on the final run also made it more difficult to maximise the lap. The car itself is not in a bad place, but there are a few areas for us to understand better. “We’ll go through everything tonight and focus on putting ourselves in the best position possible for tomorrow’s race.” George Russell on Antonelli behind him 11:14 , Kieran Jackson "You can't discount Kimi," Russell says."You know, started 19th in Monza and now he's in 16th, so, yeah, he should be leading by a few laps early this time." George (Russell) has been very strong since the first lap of FP1, but Charles did a good job to put the car on the front row. “On Lewis’ side, it was difficult to get a tow because the different run plans made it complicated to synchronise with the other cars.
